Monday 12th October 2026, 14:15. Visit 3 of a 2/52 plan.

Mrs Bell ("call me Rosie, hen") is a 77-year-old lady with type 2 diabetes on metformin alone (last HbA1c 52 mmol/mol on 02/09/2026, no known retinopathy, nephropathy or neuropathy), seen for a healing dog bite to the right shin. History from Mrs Bell and Callum: on 05/10/26 she was bitten by a dog in the back court while putting out the bins. The dog, a Staffordshire bull terrier called Tyson, belongs to her landlord, Duncan, who runs Moss & Kerr Lettings (0141 332 6045); Mr Moss has since moved the dog to a relative's. She caught her foot on the moss on the back steps as she pulled away but did not fall. Seen the same evening at Clydeside Minor Injuries Unit: wound irrigated, left open (bite), tetanus booster given, co-amoxiclav 625 mg TDS for 7/7, finishing tomorrow. Wound swab, accession MB26-0418833: light growth of Pasteurella multocida, sensitive to co-amoxiclav.

Rosie lives alone and is widowed. Retired school dinner lady at St Saviour's Primary (retired 2008). Callum calls in daily after his shift at Fairfield shipyard. Neighbour across the landing, Mrs Agnieszka "Aggie" Wójcik, keeps a spare key.

On examination: alert and chatty, walking with a stick. Right anterior shin: two puncture wounds (0.6 x 0.4 cm and 0.5 x 0.5 cm) and a 3.2 cm superficial laceration, edges approximating; 80% granulation, 20% slough, minimal serous exudate. Erythema now 1 cm from wound edge (was 4 cm on 07/10/26, pen-marked). No tracking, fluctuance or crepitus; calf soft and non-tender. Pedal pulses palpable, ABPI 0.98 R / 1.02 L. Monofilament 10/10 sites both feet. T 36.9, P 82, BP 146/82, capillary glucose 9.4 mmol/L. Old Bell's palsy (2015) with mild residual left facial weakness, unchanged.

Her sugars rose into the 12s while on the antibiotic; diary reviewed and she is back to usual levels today.

Plan: wound cleansed with saline, Inadine and a bordered foam dressing applied, change three times weekly. Finish co-amoxiclav as prescribed. Leg elevation when sitting. SBAR to Dr Nandakumar re: glucose readings. Next visit Thursday 15/10/2026. Advised Mrs Bell to call 111 if spreading redness, fever or increasing pain.

Siobhán MacLeòid, Staff Nurse (District Nursing)
